_note: The five team roles (Ace, Sweeper, Support, Wall, Tank; v2, D-078) and the build-name ladder. Every rule and number lives here; trainers/team_roles.py and its browser copy (app/web/28_teamroles.html) only evaluate them. Each role answers one competitive question from the same one-on-ones against the generation's Elite Four and Champions, both sides at level 100 (docs/design/V2_PLAN.md §5). The 34 roles in roles.json stay as the second layer underneath. Words shown as ⟨…⟩ are placeholders until Zack names them (docs/naming/NAMES_NEEDED.md).
_fetch_rounds: How many times a fight may go back to the damage calculator for numbers it hadn't fetched (a Calm Mind set facing a booster needs one per boost stage). A fight still unsettled after this reads as an error, never a guess.
_level_note: Zack, 2026-10-20: both sides at level 100 for the Ace test.
_field_evs_note: The two sides' EVs. The Elite Four's and Champions' Pokémon fight with no EVs (battle/grid.py ZERO_EVS), which is how the Ace count Zack accepted in D-064 was made. One of our builds with no recorded EVs gets the standard 85 in every stat in fights (D-061), and blank EVs count as no evidence for any role (B19). There used to be a field_evs_each: 85 setting here that nothing read; it was removed in Phase 0 of the master plan so the file says what the engine does.

neutral._note: Zack: neutral = no type advantage either way (1x). The team lab's type read uses it.

pools._note: Named pools: the trainers whose Pokémon the Ace test fights, per generation. Every team, rematches included (Zack: don't skip any rematch). The same Pokémon with the same set counts once.

roles._v2: v2 (D-078, Zack: 'rework kind of what goes into exactly what defines those ... take the reign'): Sweeper, Wall and Support are read from the fights themselves rather than the role engine's composite scores, Tank is new, and every role keeps its numbers so the page can show its work. Ace is unchanged (D-064). Thresholds were set against every library and competitive build (docs/roles/ROLE_SCORES.md).

ace.name: Ace
ace.rule: Beats at least 80% of the Elite Four's Pokémon and 70% of the Champions' Pokémon one-on-one, both sides at level 100, in the battle engine (battle/evaluate.py: our best plan against their game AI).
ace._score_note: The score is the plain mean of the two win rates (team_roles.py ace()). It's shown, not used to decide: Ace is earned only when both rates clear their bars.

top_tier.name: Joker
top_tier._note: The tier above Ace. Zack named it Joker (2026-10-21, D-064), well below Ash's Pikachu. Off until it has a rule; Zack is fine with how many builds earn Ace.

ace.explain: The one you build the run around: it beats the League one-on-one.
ace.question: Can you build the run around it?

sweeper.name: Sweeper
sweeper.question: Once it gets going, does it take several down in a row?
sweeper.explain: Fast and strong enough to knock out one opponent after another: it moves first, 2HKOs nearly all of the League and OHKOs a good share of it.
sweeper.rule: Moves first against at least 80% of the Elite Four's and Champions' Pokémon, its best attack is a guaranteed 2HKO on at least 80% of them, and a guaranteed OHKO on at least 30%. If it carries a setup move, one use of it is applied (an estimate: the stat stage's multiplier on its Speed and on the damage).
sweeper.boost: one use of its best setup move for each stat, capped at +2
sweeper._why: Smogon's sense of a sweeper: after a boost it outspeeds and KOs much of the field. 'Moves first' compares Speed with items (Choice Scarf) as the fights do; a tie isn't first. Priority isn't counted here: it's the Priority Finisher badge.
sweeper._calibrated: 2026-10-25 over 1,076 builds (library, ecosystem and Smogon sets; the League fights with no EVs): at 60/60 465 builds qualified, at 80/80 with 30% OHKOs 246 (23%). The League's Pokémon carry no EVs, so most invested builds outspeed and 2HKO them: the OHKO share is what separates a sweeper.

support.name: Support
support.question: Does it spend its turns making the team better?
support.explain: Its moves set up the team rather than the scoreboard: hazards, removal, status, screens, healing the team, phazing, speed control. And it lives long enough to use them.
support.rule: Carries at least two support moves, and either takes two or more hits from at least 80% of the 100 hardest-hitting Elite Four and Champion attacks against it, or moves first against at least 60% of their Pokémon.
support._why: Zack: 'it has to have a move associated with that' and support needs more than one. v2 drops the role engine's score and asks instead whether it survives (or outpaces) long enough to do the job.
support._calibrated: 2026-10-25 over 1,076 builds: surviving is common against the League (the median build takes two hits from 94% of them), so the two support moves decide it: 183 builds (17%).

wall.name: Wall
wall.question: Does it take hit after hit from one side, and heal it off?
wall.explain: Built to absorb: it takes four or more hits from most of one side's strongest attacks (physical or special) and has a way to heal.
wall.rule: Takes four or more hits (the top damage roll under a third of its HP) from at least 80% of the 50 hardest-hitting physical attacks the Elite Four and Champions have against it, or of the 50 hardest special ones; and carries reliable recovery, Rest or Wish, or holds Leftovers (Black Sludge for a Poison type).
wall._why: Competitive walls are specialised (a physical wall, a special wall) and need recovery to keep walling; v1 required both sides at once. Without sustain the score is shown at 85% and the role isn't earned.

tank.name: Tank
tank.question: Does it take hits from both sides, and hit back?
tank.explain: Bulky on both sides and still dangerous: it takes three or more hits from most of the League's hardest attacks and 2HKOs most of them back. It doesn't need to heal.
tank.rule: Takes three or more hits (the top roll under half its HP) from at least 75% of the 100 hardest-hitting Elite Four and Champion attacks against it, and its best attack is a guaranteed 2HKO on at least 60% of their Pokémon (no boosts).
tank._why: New in v2 (Zack: 'I want to add Tank'). Smogon's tank is a bulky attacker: it trades hits rather than avoiding or healing them. Three hits rather than the Wall's four, and it has to hit back.

pivot.name: Pivot
pivot.question: Does it keep the team's momentum, coming in safely and handing off to the right teammate?
pivot.explain: It switches in on an attack it can take and goes out with something to show for it: U-turn or Baton Pass to bring a teammate in safely, or a switch-in ability (Intimidate, Natural Cure) that makes every entry pay. Smogon's pivot.
pivot.rule: Carries a pivoting move (U-turn, Baton Pass) and either takes two or more hits from at least 80% of the 100 hardest-hitting Elite Four and Champion attacks against it or moves first against at least 80% of their Pokémon; or has Intimidate or Natural Cure and takes those two hits.
pivot._why: New in v2.3 (Zack, 2026-10-26: 'I also think pivot needs to be added to the list of team roles'). The role engine's own pivot archetype (trainers/roles.json) reads the same tools; this one asks the League fights whether it can make the entry.
pivot._calibrated: 2026-10-26 over 1,076 builds: 66 carry a pivoting move and 60 a switch-in ability; 130 earn it at these bars (12%; switch-in abilities include each species' default first ability). The League carries no EVs, so nearly every pivoting-move user clears the bulk-or-speed bar: the tool is what separates a Pivot, the bar keeps out the frail ones.

roles._score: Each role's score is 0-1 and shown, not used to decide (each role is earned only when every bar is cleared). Ace: the mean of its two win rates. Sweeper and Tank need two things at once, so their score is the geometric mean of the two shares (a Pokémon strong at one and hopeless at the other scores low). Wall: its better side's share, at 85% without sustain. Support: its support moves (three or more count fully) times how well it lasts (half for showing up, half for surviving or moving first).

_overrides: Team roles set by hand, once Zack approves them (D-059: computed, and hand-overridable). {"<build id>": {"<ace|wall|sweeper|support>": true or false, "why": "..."}}. Earned follows the override; the score stays computed and the read says it was set by hand. The Pokémon lab tries overrides in the browser and copies them out in this shape.

naming._note: Zack's ladder. 'Match' is the build's primary role score in the role engine (roles.json). The stronger the match, the fewer words the name needs. Below the last band the build has no name yet. Two or three roles at 0.80 or more get a hybrid noun from the hybrids table (it grows as builds need it).
naming.type_from: first type of the species in the build's generation

movesets._note: The first archetype whose test passes describes the moveset. Tests count moves by role-engine category.

words._note: Zack fills these in; an empty value shows the placeholder ⟨id⟩. type.<Type>, noun.<role id>, hybrid.<role ids sorted, joined by +>, moveset.<id>, team_role.<ace|wall|sweeper|support|none>, bst.<id>, unnamed. team_shape.<id> and line.<line id> too.

team._note: The team homepage's reads (v2): the scouting report (strengths, weaknesses, tendencies) draws on these checks; add one and the report reads it (app/web/84_teamlab.html evaluates the kinds below). The checks were v1's scenario questions.

questions.ask: Can this six beat every Champion Pokémon one-on-one?
questions.rule: each Champion Pokémon is beaten one-on-one (level 100) by at least one of the six

questions.ask: Can this six beat every Elite Four Pokémon one-on-one?
questions.rule: each Elite Four Pokémon is beaten one-on-one (level 100) by at least one of the six

questions.ask: Is any attacking type a problem for three or more of them, with nobody resisting it?
questions.rule: three or more weak to it, none resist or are immune

questions.ask: Is there a type nobody hits super-effectively?
questions.rule: single types no attack of the six hits for more than neutral

questions.ask: Who outspeeds a base-100 Speed Pokémon at level 100?
questions.rule: its Speed (neutral nature, 31 IVs, 85 EVs unless recorded) beats a base-100 at the same spread

questions.ask: Does the team set or clear entry hazards?
questions.rule: at least one hazard or Rapid Spin move

questions.ask: Who can heal itself or the team?
questions.rule: recovery, Rest, Wish or Heal Bell-style moves

questions.ask: Who stops a Dragon Dance or Swords Dance sweeper?
Does the team have each team role?
questions.rule: at least one of the six earns each role

shapes._note: The team's shape (v2): the first archetype whose needs the six meet names it, in this order. Each shows how close the team is to every other one. Roles are counted by who earns them; features (weather, Trick Room, Baton Pass, hazards) by the moves and abilities the six carry. naming.words.team_shape names them.

trick_room.label: Trick Room
trick_room.explain: Slow, strong Pokémon behind a Trick Room setter: the slowest moves first for five turns.

weather.label: weather
weather.explain: A weather setter and the Pokémon that thrive in it (Swift Swim, Chlorophyll, sand or hail).

baton_pass.label: Baton Pass
baton_pass.explain: Boosts built up by one Pokémon and passed to the next.

hyper_offense.label: hyper offense
hyper_offense.explain: Almost all attackers, hazards up front, little defence: win before they can.

stall.label: stall
stall.explain: Walls and support that wear the other side down with status and hazards.

semi_stall.label: semi-stall
semi_stall.explain: A defensive core with one or two win conditions.

bulky_offense.label: bulky offense
bulky_offense.explain: Attackers that can take a hit: tanks and sweepers together.

offense.label: offense
offense.explain: Mostly attackers, with a little support.

balance.label: balance
balance.explain: Offence and defence in equal parts: anything the others don't fit.
